humanQuestions.question: The rest of PLAN P1-1 (the contracts of `sim.run` / `board.run` and the second record of `correctness.check`) needs the owner's reading of #5 A-7 against FR-1, FR-9 and FR-10 (OD-18 sub-question 7), for the first backend `cpu_standin` only. A-7 names one "run" in its loop; FR-1 has a sim step and a board step, and FR-9 has the correctness check "at both points"; `cpu_standin` has one kind of experiment, the compiled kernel run on the CPU. (1) Under which HW tool is that experiment offered: (a) `board.run` only - the backend does not offer `sim.run`; (b) `sim.run` only - it does not offer `board.run`; (c) both, each carrying out the same local run; (d) something else (name it)? (2) If (1) leaves a point the target does not offer (a call there answers the reserved kind `not_offered`, ADR-0016), what does the round loop of FR-1 do: (a) it skips that step and the rules FR-1 gives the remaining point apply unchanged (board only: a failed check drops the candidate, there is no repair return and no promotion filter; sim only: a failed check returns to code generation, and the sim measurement is what the round evaluates and records); (b) it skips that step and the one point takes both roles (a failed check returns to code generation up to the repair bound and then drops the candidate; its measurement is the final one); (c) another rule (name it)? (3) Correctness on `cpu_standin`: (a) one check per attempt, at the one offered point; (b) two checks per attempt, one as the sim-point check and one as the board-point check, also where both are the same local run? If two: does FR-9's "동일 검증을 반복한다" mean (i) the same procedure with inputs drawn anew for each check (the reading ADR-0021 decision 3 took), or (ii) the same drawn inputs at both points? (4) The mock backend (FR-10: contract tests): may a run whose hw_profile names the mock be answered by the first case's `correctness.check` contract - the oracle of the HQ-0004 answer, and the `tolerance` member of `instance.json` read with the meaning it has for `cpu_standin` - so that the contract tests of P1-1 run the judging over the mock: (a) yes; (b) no, the mock gets its own rule (name it)? Not asked here: anything about a real simulator or board (#5 B-2, B-3), the promotion rule and k (OD-15, OD-29), the objective (#5 A-4), `profiler.collect`, `blob.push` / `blob.fetch`, budgets and spend (OD-2, OD-19), recovery after a failure (OD-10), and the oracle or tolerance of any other backend beyond (4).
humanQuestions.decision: (1)(c), (2) not applicable, (3)(b)(i), (4)(a) — owner reply https://github.com/myungjoo/HIL-Claw/issues/5#issuecomment-6117798837: `cpu_standin` offers both `sim.run` and `board.run`; in the first case (the owner's local PC, native build and run) the two carry out the same local run and nothing but the execution point distinguishes them. Foreseen and not decided: a configuration in which the board is a machine of a non-native ISA and `sim.run` is an emulated run of the board's ISA on the local host (e.g. aarch64 under qemu-user on x86-64) — it needs an emulator (new external dependency, A-13), a hw_profile for a kernel built on one machine and run on another (ADR-0035 Boundaries, OD-4) and remote access (#5 B-2); to be registered as an open point and settled with those, not in T-0088. The rule for a target that lacks a point (OD-26; StandardScenarios S1-b) is not answered. Correctness: two checks per attempt, one as the sim-point check and one as the board-point check, also where both are the same local run; the same harness, predicate and tolerance with inputs drawn anew for each check (the reading of ADR-0021 decision 3 is confirmed, not reopened); how a call states its execution point is the record's design. Mock: a run whose hw_profile names the mock is answered by the first case's `correctness.check` contract (the oracle of the HQ-0004 answer, the `tolerance` member of `instance.json` with the meaning of ADR-0020 decision 2), so that the contract tests of P1-1 run the whole judging over the mock; the mock's script stands in for the kernel, not for the reference — it may compute the product for the seed of the call, the reference stays with the tool function; what the default script answers is the second record's.
